title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄序
皇上躬聖資繼照當天改元萬曆
適海內當大比士貢之於
廷易曰飛龍在天利見大人甚盛
際也其在四川巡按御史孫
代監臨試事先是巡按監察
御史孫〔濟遠〕禮聘四方文學
===
之官陸逾錫閣水瀬巴渝以
次畢集於是以〔廷陳〕暨學正
蕭〔雲鵠〕爲考試官教授彭〔時〕
中教諭劉〔憲〕廖〔守俊〕爲同考
試官提調則左布政使羅〔瑤〕
右布政使馮〔成能〕監試則按
察使徐〔行〕副使林〔舜道〕暨百
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄序

皇上躬聖資，繼照當天，改元萬曆。適海內當大比，士貢之於廷。《易》曰：「飛龍在天，利見大人。」甚盛際也。其在四川，巡按御史孫代監臨試事。先是，巡按監察御史孫〔濟遠〕禮聘四方文學之官，陸逾錫閣，水瀬巴渝，以次畢集。於是以〔廷陳〕暨學正蕭〔雲鵠〕爲考試官，教授彭〔時〕中、教諭劉〔憲〕、廖〔守俊〕爲同考試官。提調則左布政使羅〔瑤〕、右布政使馮〔成能〕；監試則按察使徐〔行〕、副使林〔舜道〕暨百
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

His Majesty, endowed with sagely qualities, succeeded to the throne in continuing radiance and inaugurated the Wanli era. It happened that the triennial examination was due throughout the realm, with scholars to be recommended to the court. The Book of Changes says: “The flying dragon is in the heavens; it is beneficial to see the great man.” This was indeed a most flourishing occasion. In Sichuan, Regional Inspector Sun acted as Supervising Official for the examination. Previously, the Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, Sun Jiyuan, had courteously invited educational officials from various places. Crossing Xige [?] by land and traversing the rapids of Bayu by water, they all arrived in succession.

Thereupon, Tingchen and Xiao Yunhu, an Instructor, were appointed Examiners; Peng Shizhong, a Prefectural School Professor, and Liu Xian and Liao Shoujun, both County School Instructors, were appointed Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Luo Yao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Feng Chengneng, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Xu Xing, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Lin Shundao, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, together with all …

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
執事咸愼選以充乃進提學
副使管〔大勳〕所簡士二千有
奇三試之而得雋者七十人
錄其文以
獻
〔廷陳〕不佞當首序以敬戒多士
序曰竊聞之岷山之精上應
井絡
===
帝以會昌神以建福於休哉非遇
其時此何以稱焉洪惟我
皇上應運中興沛然
明詔正人心興治道開蕩平之路
以與天下更始蜀在西南隅
至險遠矣山谷龐眉耆耇之
老咸稱睹至和焉雨暘時而
punctuated:
執事咸愼選以充，乃進提學副使管〔大勳〕所簡士二千有奇，三試之而得雋者七十人，錄其文以獻。
〔廷陳〕不佞，當首序以敬戒多士。序曰：「竊聞之，岷山之精，上應井絡；帝以會昌，神以建福。於休哉！非遇其時，此何以稱焉？洪惟我皇上應運中興，沛然明詔，正人心，興治道，開蕩平之路，以與天下更始。蜀在西南隅，至險遠矣。山谷龐眉耆耇之老，咸稱睹至和焉。雨暘時而
translation_en:
…all the functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. Then the more than two thousand scholars selected by Guan Daxun 管大勳, Vice Commissioner for Education, were admitted. After three examination sessions, seventy outstanding candidates were selected, and their compositions were transcribed for presentation to the throne.
I, Tingchen 廷陳, untalented though I am, am charged with providing the opening preface, respectfully to admonish the assembled scholars. The preface reads: “I have heard that the spiritual essence of Mount Min corresponds above to the celestial region of the Well constellation. The Lord on High brings prosperity at the appointed conjunction, and the spirits bestow blessings. How splendid! Without encountering the proper time, how could this be spoken of?
“Magnificent indeed is our August Emperor, who has responded to Heaven’s destiny and brought about a restoration. His enlightened edicts issue abundantly, rectifying people’s hearts, promoting the way of good government, and opening a broad and level road, so as to make a fresh beginning with all under Heaven. Shu lies in the southwestern corner, exceedingly rugged and remote. Yet the venerable, bushy-browed elders of its mountains and valleys all declare that they have witnessed perfect harmony. Rain and sunshine come at their proper seasons, and…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
年轂登戎㚟不順者徂征而
品彙懽忻沐於膏澤斯其會
也昌乎以建福於民氓寧有
旣乎乃多士獨得以此時進
何其遇也古今稱蜀之盛若
天門地簸包玉壘控瞿塘山
雄乎五嶽而江冠於四瀆斯
===
形勝也然以語乎大一統則
偏矣火井丹砂江珠瑕英絲
枲斑彩衣被乎天下斯土之
毛善利也然以語乎富有則
眇矣夫
皇上任賢圖治而賢臣以人事君
誠得西南士濟濟乎足以供
punctuated: 年轂登，戎㚟不順者徂征，而品彙懽忻，沐於膏澤。斯其會也，昌乎？以建福於民氓，寧有旣乎？乃多士獨得以此時進，何其遇也！古今稱蜀之盛，若天門、地簸，包玉壘，控瞿塘，山雄乎五嶽，而江冠於四瀆，斯形勝也；然以語乎大一統則偏矣。火井、丹砂、江珠、瑕英、絲枲、斑彩，衣被乎天下，斯土之毛善利也；然以語乎富有則眇矣。夫皇上任賢圖治，而賢臣以人事君，誠得西南士濟濟乎足以供
translation_en: …the yearly harvests are abundant, the unruly Western Rong and Southern Man [?] are marched against in punitive expeditions, and the myriad creatures rejoice, bathed in rich grace. Is not this convergence prosperous indeed? In establishing blessings for the common folk, could there ever be an end? That the many scholars alone are able to advance at such a time—what good fortune they have met with! Past and present accounts praising the splendor of Shu cite Heaven's Gate (Tianmen) and Earth's Winnowing Fan (Dibo), its encompassing of Mount Yulei and command of Qutang Gorge, its mountains more majestic than the Five Marchmounts and its river heading the Four Great Waterways—such is its strategic topography; yet when spoken of in relation to the Great Unity of the empire, it is merely one corner. Its fire wells, cinnabar, river pearls, flawed-jade gems, silk, hemp, and variegated brocades clothe and benefit the entire realm—such are the fine and profitable products of its soil; yet when spoken of in relation to the empire's boundless wealth, they are trifling. Now, His Majesty employs the worthy to plan for good governance, and worthy ministers serve the ruler by recommending capable men. If we truly obtain a multitude of flourishing scholars from the southwest sufficient to supply…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
國家之用其盛也孰能尚之粤
在漢初五星聚東井說者謂
文章之盛炳焉與三代同風
乃其立學興士寔自蜀郡文
翁始考文翁之在當時作禮
殿以祀先聖先賢遣子弟高
等受經博士絃誦之聲比於
===
齊魯意至勤厚矣顧其後最
著名者司馬相如王褒之徒
僅以文章顯而聖賢之學無
聞焉毋乃與初指背謬歟若
我
祖宗設科非聖賢之行不以迪士
所重者欲得眞材以裨實用
punctuated: 國家之用，其盛也孰能尚之？粤在漢初，五星聚東井，說者謂文章之盛，炳焉與三代同風。乃其立學興士，寔自蜀郡文翁始。考文翁之在當時，作禮殿以祀先聖先賢，遣子弟高等受經博士，絃誦之聲，比於齊、魯，意至勤厚矣。顧其後最著名者，司馬相如、王褒之徒，僅以文章顯，而聖賢之學無聞焉，毋乃與初指背謬歟？若我祖宗設科，非聖賢之行不以迪士，所重者欲得眞材以裨實用。
translation_en: …the needs of the state—what could surpass such flourishing! Looking back to the beginning of the Han dynasty, when the five planets converged in the Eastern Well (Dongjing) constellation, commentators said that the flourishing of literature shone brightly in the same manner as that of the Three Dynasties. Yet the establishment of schools and the promotion of scholars there actually began with Wen Weng 文翁 of Shu Commandery (Shujun 蜀郡). Examining Wen Weng in his own time, he built a ceremonial hall to offer sacrifices to the former sages and former worthies, and dispatched youths of the highest caliber to receive instruction in the Classics from Erudites (boshi). The sound of stringed instruments and chanting rivaled that of Qi 齊 and Lu 魯; his intentions were most diligent and generous. However, those who became most famous afterward—men of the ilk of Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 and Wang Bao 王褒—distinguished themselves merely through literary composition, while nothing was heard of the learning of the sages and worthies. Was this not contrary to his original aim? As for our Imperial Ancestors' establishment of the examination system, they did not guide scholars with anything other than the conduct of the sages and worthies; what they valued was obtaining men of true talent to aid in practical use. …

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
今御史亦惓惓與多士約惟
此初非獨以文章命之也乃
今縱觀多士所自獻明經術
則原本道德語事變則揚搉
古今郁郁斌斌卽齊魯能言
之士不讓此非皆有志於學
聖賢者與夫使誠有志於學
===
聖賢卽才爲眞才用爲實用
異日者坐策乎
廊廟足以任
社稷之安危分寄乎疆場足以係
生民之休戚助
維新之化流永世之聲使學士
大夫慕之曰斯蜀產也斯崛
punctuated: 今御史亦惓惓與多士約，惟此初非獨以文章命之也。乃今縱觀多士所自獻，明經術則原本道德，語事變則揚搉古今，郁郁斌斌，卽齊魯能言之士不讓，此非皆有志於學聖賢者與？夫使誠有志於學聖賢，卽才爲眞才，用爲實用。異日者，坐策乎廊廟，足以任社稷之安危；分寄乎疆場，足以係生民之休戚。助維新之化，流永世之聲，使學士大夫慕之曰：「斯蜀產也，斯崛
translation_en: Now the Censor also earnestly makes this covenant with the many scholars, for from the beginning he did not instruct them solely in terms of literary composition. Yet now, surveying all that the scholars have presented, in elucidating the classical arts they trace things back to theWay and its Virtue, and in discussing changing events they weigh and assess antiquity and the present. Richly cultured and refined in both substance and form, they do not yield even to the eloquent scholars of Qi and Lu. Are these not all men who aspire to learn from the sages and worthies? Now, if they truly aspire to learn from the sages and worthies, then their talent will be genuine talent, and their usefulness will be practical usefulness. In days to come, seated planning in the court, they will be equal to bearing the safety and peril of the altars of soil and grain; entrusted with responsibilities on the frontiers, they will be equal to holding the weal and woe of the people in the balance. They will assist the transforming influence of the dynastic renewal and leave behind a reputation for eternal generations, causing scholars and grandees to admire them and say: "These are natives of Shu [Sichuan]; these are men who rose up…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
起於萬曆之初者也豈直地
之形稱勝而土之毛善利哉
主司何幸獲藉以爲榮也有
如不然視文爲弁髦曰苟緣
是以干祿位華吾躬肥吾家
而止矣鄙哉是利之也執市
之民可舉何必士如此才卽
非眞乃僞也用卽不實乃虛
也虛與僞悉邪也夫
===
明詔方以正人心爲亟而萬一者
以邪進柰辱主司何斯其背
繆不益甚歟豈獨有媿於蜀
土地將負茲萬曆之
昌會而無以徼福於神明也寧可
punctuated: 起於萬曆之初者也！」豈直地之形稱勝，而土之毛善利哉？主司何幸，獲藉以爲榮也。有如不然，視文爲弁髦，曰：「苟緣是以干祿位，華吾躬、肥吾家而止矣。」鄙哉！是利之也，執市之民可舉，何必士？如此，才卽非眞，乃僞也；用卽不實，乃虛也。虛與僞，悉邪也。夫明詔方以正人心爲亟，而萬一者以邪進，柰辱主司何？斯其背繆不益甚歟？豈獨有媿於蜀土地，將負茲萬曆之昌會，而無以徼福於神明也。寧可
translation_en:
…who rose to prominence at the beginning of the Wanli era!” Would it then merely be that the topography of the land is celebrated as magnificent and the produce of its soil is good for profit? How fortunate we, the chief examiners, would be to derive honor through them!

If, on the contrary, they regard literary learning as a cast-off cap, saying: “If I can just use this to seek emolument and rank, to glorify my own person and enrich my own family, that is enough”—how base! This is to treat it as mere profit; one might as well recommend people from the marketplace, so why must it be scholars? If they are like this, then their talent is not genuine, but false; their utility is not substantial, but hollow. Hollowness and falsity are altogether heterodox. Now, the Radiant Edict is just making the rectification of men’s minds an urgent priority, yet if by some remote chance anyone advances through heterodoxy, what can be done about the disgrace brought upon the chief examiners? Would such perversity and error not be even more extreme? Not only would they bring shame upon the land of Shu, they would also betray this flourishing occasion of the Wanli reign and have no way to seek blessings from the gods and spirits. How could one…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
不重懼乎昔益州刺史講德
託之鹿鳴之歌且曰雷霆必
發而潛底震動枹鼓鏗鏘而
介士奮竦故物不震不發士
不激不勇〔廷陳〕茲聽歌鹿鳴
恭際
飛龍之盛義不可不正言以激多
===
士有告者曰蜀居坤方爲文
爲臣得順理之性名公卿史
牒相望士何詎弗勇於聖賢
乎果然則〔廷陳〕之激之也又
多乎哉維時巡撫地方則右
僉都御史曾〔省吾〕兼督川東
則右副都御史蔡〔文〕巡理茶
punctuated:
不重懼乎？昔益州刺史講德，託之《鹿鳴》之歌，且曰：「雷霆必發而潛底震動，枹鼓鏗鏘而介士奮竦。故物不震不發，士不激不勇。」〔廷陳〕茲聽歌《鹿鳴》，恭際飛龍之盛，義不可不正言以激多士。有告者曰：「蜀居坤方，爲文爲臣，得順理之性，名公卿史牒相望，士何詎弗勇於聖賢乎？」果然，則〔廷陳〕之激之也，又多乎哉！

維時巡撫地方則右僉都御史曾〔省吾〕，兼督川東則右副都御史蔡〔文〕，巡理茶
translation_en:
… not deeply dread this? In antiquity, the Regional Inspector of Yizhou, in expounding upon virtue, entrusted his message to the song of "Luming" [The Cry of the Deer], and moreover said: "When thunderbolts inevitably strike, the hidden depths are shaken into motion; when drumsticks and drums clang and resound, armored warriors rouse themselves and stand ready. Thus, if things are not shaken, they do not burst forth; if scholars are not stirred, they are not courageous." As I, Tingchen, now listen to the singing of "Luming" and reverently encounter this flourishing age of the Flying Dragon, in duty I cannot but speak forthrightly to stir the many scholars. Someone told me: "Shu is situated in the direction of Kun [the southwest]; in creating literature and in serving as ministers, its people attain a nature that accords with principle. Renowned high ministers and nobles appear one after another in the historical records—how could its scholars fail to be courageous in aspiring to become sages and worthies?" If this is truly so, then is my stirring of them even excessive!

At this time, serving as Grand Coordinator of the region was Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right Zeng Xingwu; concurrently directing Eastern Sichuan was Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right Cai Wen; inspecting and administering the tea…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
法則監察御史趙〔煥　〕若刑部
員外郎鄭〔恭　〕奉
命適至而左叅政王〔宮用〕左叅議
韓〔宰　〕右叅議沈〔伯龍〕副使范
〔燧　〕林〔應節〕楊〔芷　〕〔江　〕僉事李
〔與善〕周〔思充〕秦〔舜翰〕丘〔文學〕
署都指揮僉事胡〔恩　〕徐〔仁威〕
===
趙〔鵬　〕皆綜理防範於外右叅
政陳〔善道〕僉事張〔思忠〕先期
入
賀于法皆得書書之
江西臨江府儒學教授周〔廷　〕
〔陳　〕謹序
punctuated:
法則監察御史趙〔煥　〕，若刑部員外郎鄭〔恭　〕奉命適至；而左叅政王〔宮用〕、左叅議韓〔宰　〕、右叅議沈〔伯龍〕，副使范〔燧　〕、林〔應節〕、楊〔芷　〕、〔江　〕，僉事李〔與善〕、周〔思充〕、秦〔舜翰〕、丘〔文學〕，署都指揮僉事胡〔恩　〕、徐〔仁威〕、趙〔鵬　〕，皆綜理防範於外；右叅政陳〔善道〕、僉事張〔思忠〕先期入賀，于法皆得書，書之。

江西臨江府儒學教授周〔廷　〕〔陳　〕謹序。
translation_en:
… regulations was Investigating Censor Zhao Huan 趙煥; and Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice Zheng Gong 鄭恭, bearing an imperial command, had just arrived. Meanwhile, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Gongyong 王宮用, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Han Zai 韓宰, and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Shen Bolong 沈伯龍; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Fan Sui 范燧, Lin Yingjie 林應節, Yang Zhi 楊芷, and [?] Jiang 江 [?]; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Li Yushan 李與善, Zhou Sichong 周思充, Qin Shunhan 秦舜翰, and Qiu Wenxue 丘文學; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Hu En 胡恩, Xu Renwei 徐仁威, and Zhao Peng 趙鵬 all oversaw the management and security precautions in the outer compound. Right Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Shandao 陳善道 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Sizhong 張思忠 had departed ahead of time to present felicitations at court. By rule, all of them are entitled to be recorded, and so I record them.

Respectfully prefaced by Zhou Tingchen 周廷陳, Instructor in the Confucian School of Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
萬曆元年四川鄉試
監臨官
巡按四川監察御史孫　代〔紹甫陜西扶風縣人　已未進士〕
提調官
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使羅　瑶〔國華湖廣巴陵縣人　庚戌進士〕

四川等處提刑按察司副使林舜道〔允中福建閩縣人　已未進士〕
===
考試官
江西臨江府儒學教授周廷陳〔大謨直隸績溪縣人　乙卯貢士〕
湖廣荊州府歸州儒學學正蕭雲鵠〔志邁福建晉江縣人　辛酉貢士〕
同考試官
浙江處州府儒學教授彭時中〔體和直隸石埭縣人　壬子貢士〕

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
林放問禮之本子曰大哉問禮與其奢也
寧儉
體物而不可遺使天下之人齊明盛服以
承祭祀洋洋乎如在其上如在其左右
詩曰神之格思不可度思矧可射思
其爲氣也至大至剛
易
===
上九自天祐之吉无不利
利有攸往中正有慶利涉大川木道乃行
益動而巽日進无疆天施地生其益无
方凡益之道與時偕行
是故形而上者謂之道形而下者謂之器
化而裁之謂之變推而行之謂之通舉
而措之天下之民謂之事業
乾以君之
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

林放問禮之本。子曰：「大哉問！禮，與其奢也，寧儉。」
體物而不可遺。使天下之人齊明盛服，以承祭祀。洋洋乎！如在其上，如在其左右。《詩》曰：「神之格思，不可度思！矧可射思？」
其爲氣也，至大至剛。

易

上九：自天祐之，吉无不利。
利有攸往，中正有慶。利涉大川，木道乃行。益動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。
是故形而上者謂之道，形而下者謂之器，化而裁之謂之變，推而行之謂之通，舉而措之天下之民謂之事業。
乾以君之。

書
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

Lin Fang asked about the fundamental principle of ritual. The Master said, "A great question indeed! In festive ceremonies, it is better to be frugal than extravagant."
They enter into all things, and nothing is without them. They cause all people in the world to fast, purify themselves, and don their finest robes to perform the sacrifices. How overflowing they are! They seem to be above them, and to be on their left and right. The Book of Odes (Shi) says, "The coming of the spirits cannot be surmised—how much less can they be slighted!"
This qi is supremely great and supremely刚 (unyielding).

The Book of Changes (Yi)

Top Nine: It is blessed by Heaven; auspicious, nothing is unfavorable.
"It is favorable to have somewhere to go": through centrality and correctness there will be celebration. "It is favorable to cross the great river": the way of wood is thus put into action. Increase (Yi) moves and is adaptable, advancing daily without limit. Heaven bestows and earth brings forth, so its increase knows no bounds. The way of all increase proceeds in harmony with the time.
Therefore, what is above form is called the Way (Dao); what is below form is called a concrete vessel (qi). To transform and regulate it is called change; to extend and carry it out is called free flow; to take it up and apply it to all the people in the world is called a great undertaking.
Qian rules over it.

The Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
三載考績三考黜陟幽明庶績咸熙
爾惟訓于朕志若作酒醴爾惟麴糵若作
和羹爾惟鹽梅
曰雨曰霽曰蒙曰驛曰克
茲惟三公論道經邦燮理陰陽官不必備
惟其人
詩
七月食瓜八月斷壺
===
菁菁者莪在彼中阿既見君子樂且有儀
菁菁者莪在彼中沚既見君子我心則
喜菁菁者莪在彼中陵既見君子錫我
百朋
穆穆文王於緝熙敬止假哉天命
撻彼殷武奮伐荊楚罙入其阻裒荊之旅
有截其所湯孫之緒
春秋
盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕
punctuated:
帝曰：「咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。」三載考績，三考，黜陟幽明，庶績咸熙。
爾惟訓于朕志。若作酒醴，爾惟麴糵；若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。
曰雨，曰霽，曰蒙，曰驛，曰克。
茲惟三公，論道經邦，燮理陰陽，官不必備，惟其人。
《詩》
七月食瓜，八月斷壺。
菁菁者莪，在彼中阿。既見君子，樂且有儀。菁菁者莪，在彼中沚。既見君子，我心則喜。菁菁者莪，在彼中陵。既見君子，錫我百朋。
穆穆文王，於緝熙敬止！假哉天命。
撻彼殷武，奮伐荊楚。罙入其阻，裒荊之旅。有截其所，湯孫之緒。
《春秋》
盟于召陵。〔僖公四年〕
translation_en:
The Emperor said: "Ah! You twenty-two men, be reverent! Aid in the timely accomplishment of Heaven's work." Every three years there was an examination of merits, and after three examinations the undeserving were degraded and the deserving promoted, whereby all achievements flourished.

"Do you instruct me in my aims. Suppose I am making sweet wine, you are the leaven and malt; suppose I am making well-seasoned soup, you are the salt and plums."

"They are called rain, clearing up, cloudiness, disconnection, and crossing."

"These are the Three Dukes, who discuss the Way to govern the state and harmonize the yin and yang. The offices need not always be filled, save when there is the right man."

Book of Odes (Shi)

In the seventh month they eat melons; in the eighth month they cut down the bottle-gourds.

Lush grows the tarragon, in the midst of that great mound. Having seen the noble man, we are joyful and observe courtesy. Lush grows the tarragon, in the midst of that islet. Having seen the noble man, my heart is glad. Lush grows the tarragon, in the midst of that high hill. Having seen the noble man, he bestows on me a hundred sets of cowries.

August was King Wen; oh, continuously bright was his reverence! Great was the Mandate of Heaven.

Swift was that martial king of Yin, who vigorously attacked Jing-Chu. Deeply he penetrated its fastnesses, and gathered the hosts of Jing. Brought to order was its territory—such was the achievement of Tang's descendant.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

They made a covenant at Shaoling. [Fourth year of Duke Xi]

天無私覆地無私載日月無私照

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
者率是道焉無論矣漢唐而下英君誼
辟亦有仁孝聞於天下賜相國劒履上
殿者有表章六經御書飛白者其於帝
王爲學之大端果盡歟否歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
聖德淵源不可窺涘其見諸洪範註者曰敘彛
倫立皇極論家人者曰在誠實而有威
嚴以至隆禮大儒或稱帝師或呼子房
親親賢賢之道其萬世仁義之宗乎而
又時與儒臣講書講易
===
宮中無事輒讀論語
萬幾之假或
親灑宸翰或
錫書門帖稽古博文所以合內外之道也可盡
得而頌述之歟我
皇上聰明首出冲齡嗣統嚴
郊廟之明禋加
兩宮之徽號孝思求矣
punctuated: 者率是道焉，無論矣。漢唐而下，英君誼辟亦有仁孝聞於天下、賜相國劒履上殿者，有表章《六經》、御書飛白者，其於帝王爲學之大端，果盡歟？否歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，聖德淵源，不可窺涘。其見諸《洪範註》者，曰「敘彛倫，立皇極」；論《家人》者，曰「在誠實而有威嚴」；以至隆禮大儒，或稱「帝師」，或呼「子房」，親親賢賢之道，其萬世仁義之宗乎！而又時與儒臣講《書》講《易》，宮中無事輒讀《論語》，萬幾之假，或親灑宸翰，或錫書門帖，稽古博文，所以合內外之道也，可盡得而頌述之歟？我皇上聰明首出，冲齡嗣統，嚴郊廟之明禋，加兩宮之徽號，孝思求矣；
translation_en:
… all followed this Way—that goes without saying. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, among heroic rulers and righteous monarchs there were also those whose benevolence and filial piety were renowned throughout the realm, or who granted their Cancellors the privilege of ascending the audience hall wearing sword and shoes; and there were those who honored and promoted the Six Classics, or wrote imperial calligraphy in the "flying white" (feibai) style. As for the great essentials of the learning of emperors and kings, did they truly exhaust them or not?

Reflecting deeply upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), the wellspring of his sagely virtue is so vast that its shores cannot be glimpsed. As seen in his Commentary on the "Great Plan" (Hongfan zhu), he spoke of "ordering the invariable human relationships and establishing the August Ultimate"; in discussing the "Family" (Jiaren) hexagram, he said that it "lies in sincerity and truthfulness combined with majesty and strictness." Furthermore, he accorded the highest courtesy to great Confucian scholars, sometimes calling one an "Imperial Preceptor" and sometimes addressing one as his "Zifang" (Zhang Liang). Is not his Way of loving kin and honoring the worthy the ancestral model of benevolence and righteousness for ten thousand generations! Moreover, from time to time he expounded upon the Book of Documents and the Book of Changes with his Confucian ministers, and whenever he was free of affairs in the palace he would read the Analects. In his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he would sometimes personally ply the imperial brush, or bestow calligraphed door-scrolls. His examining of antiquity and broadening of learning in letters were the means by which he united the Way of the inner and the outer—can all of this be fully recounted and praised?

Our reigning Sovereign (the Wanli Emperor), foremost in intelligence and wisdom, succeeded to the throne at a tender age. He has strictly performed the pure sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, and conferred honorable titles upon the Two Empresses Dowager—his filial thoughts are far-reaching indeed [reading 求 as 永]! …

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
平臺召對元輔隆稱尚賢篤矣
經筵日講辨難更端
起受
帝鑑圖說一一顧問本指至於
御書良臣輔政鹽梅舟楫以
賜輔臣
天翰昭回龍飛鳳翥此雖
天縱緒餘莫非內外交脩之實學也
聖學方新
===
聖心方銳將允懷仁義緝熙光明以比隆唐虞
同符
聖祖矣然臣子芹曝之心猶未已也茲欲闡明
正學敷陳要道以為
聖脩萬一之助其說何居爾多士其詳言之毋
忽
問道之大原出於天本無二也自虞庭發
精一之秘授受歷三王至孔子而大著
其體天之要亦曰一以貫之而已是學
punctuated:
平臺召對，元輔隆稱，尚賢篤矣。經筵日講，辨難更端，起受《帝鑑圖說》，一一顧問本指。至於御書「良臣輔政」、「鹽梅舟楫」以賜輔臣，天翰昭回，龍飛鳳翥。此雖天縱緒餘，莫非內外交脩之實學也。聖學方新，聖心方銳，將允懷仁義，緝熙光明，以比隆唐、虞，同符聖祖矣。然臣子芹曝之心猶未已也，茲欲闡明正學，敷陳要道，以為聖脩萬一之助，其說何居？爾多士其詳言之，毋忽。
問：道之大原出於天，本無二也。自虞庭發精一之秘，授受歷三王，至孔子而大著。其體天之要，亦曰「一以貫之」而已。是學
translation_en:
He grants audiences at the Platform (Pingtai) and addresses the Chief Grand Secretary in exalted terms—profound indeed is His esteem for the worthy! At the Classics Colloquium and the daily lectures, He engages in debate as one topic succeeds another; rising to accept the Illustrated Mirror for Emperors (Dijian tushuo), He inquiries into the essential meaning of each entry one by one. As for His writing in the imperial hand the phrases "Good ministers assist in governance" and "Salt and plum, boat and oar" to bestow upon the Grand Secretaries, the Imperial brush shines brilliantly around, with dragons flying and phoenixes soaring. Although these are but the spare refinements of His heaven-endowed genius, none of them fails to be practical learning that cultivates both the inner and the outer. Now that the Sage Learning is freshly begun and the Sage Mind is keenly focused, He will surely cherish benevolence and righteousness and continue in bright illumination, so as to rival the glory of Tang and Yu and match the standard of Our Sacred Ancestors. Yet the humble desire of subjects and sons to offer wild celery and warm sunlight is still not exhausted. Now, if one wishes to elucidate orthodox learning and set forth the essential Way in order to offer even a ten-thousandth part of assistance to the Sage Cultivation, on what arguments should this rest? You many scholars, speak of this in detail and do not be negligent.

Question: The great source of the Way comes from Heaven; originally there is no duality in it. Since the court of Yu disclosed the secret of "subtlety and unity," its transmission passed through the Three Kings, and down to Confucius it became greatly manifest. The essential principle by which he embodied Heaven was likewise simply called "threading it together with one." This learning…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
也惟顏子契之而唯於曾子授於子思
至軻之後不得其傳漢儒索之詞章訓
詁僅襲商賜之緒餘而不知孔顏授受
之微不若是支矣至宋周程繼出始能
以無欲存仁之學體天地之常而聖人
精一之旨復明於天下伊洛源流至南
宋而有朱陸二子者出皆以程氏爲宗
者然二子立論不同鵞湖辯論往復不
一其徒遂以德性問學各立門户而支
===
離頓悟之說互相訾議豈二子之學果
若是異歟抑亦有同者歟夫學必一致
而後可以入聖果二子若是其異也則
又烏得俱爲理學之宗歟自宋末以來
學者習於見聞多宗朱而斥陸近世儒
者則復表章陸氏揭本體以破羣疑而
世之講學者遂有考亭狥外之議是果
孰爲定論歟夫殊途而同歸在二子固
有各造其微非淺學所能窺者而耳食
punctuated: 也，惟顏子契之，而唯於曾子，授於子思，至軻之後，不得其傳。漢儒索之詞章訓詁，僅襲商、賜之緒餘，而不知孔、顏授受之微，不若是支矣。至宋，周、程繼出，始能以無欲存仁之學，體天地之常，而聖人精一之旨，復明於天下。伊洛源流，至南宋而有朱、陸二子者出，皆以程氏爲宗者。然二子立論不同，鵞湖辯論，往復不一，其徒遂以德性、問學各立門户，而支離、頓悟之說，互相訾議。豈二子之學，果若是異歟？抑亦有同者歟？夫學必一致，而後可以入聖。果二子若是其異也，則又烏得俱爲理學之宗歟？自宋末以來，學者習於見聞，多宗朱而斥陸；近世儒者，則復表章陸氏，揭本體以破羣疑，而世之講學者，遂有考亭狥外之議。是果孰爲定論歟？夫殊途而同歸，在二子固有各造其微，非淺學所能窺者，而耳食
translation_en: … Only Master Yan [Yan Hui 顏回] grasped it tacitly, while Master Zeng [Zeng Can 曾參] assented to it, transmitting it to Zisi 子思; after [Meng] Ke 孟軻 [Mencius], its transmission was lost. The scholars of the Han sought it in literary composition and textual exegesis, merely inheriting the residual threads of Shang [Bu Shang 卜商, Zixia] and Ci [Duanmu Ci 端木賜, Zigong], without knowing that the subtle essence transmitted between Confucius and Yan Hui was not so fragmented as this. Coming to the Song, Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] and the Chengs [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] emerged in succession. Only then were they able, through the learning of having no desires and preserving benevolence, to embody the constancy of Heaven and Earth, so that the sages' purport of refinement and singleness became clear once more throughout the realm. As the stream of the Yi and Luo rivers [the Cheng brothers' school] flowed into the Southern Song, two masters, Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] and Lu [Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵], appeared, both taking the Chengs as their ancestral standard. Yet the two masters established different arguments; in their debates at Goose Lake (Ehu 鵞湖), they went back and forth without reaching unity. Their followers consequently set up separate rival schools around "honoring the moral nature" and "following the path of inquiry and study," and with charges of "fragmentation" and "sudden enlightenment," they criticized and disparaged one another. Was the learning of the two masters truly so different as this? Or did they also have points in common? Now, learning must be unified in aim before one can enter into sagehood. If the two masters were truly so different as this, then how could both alike be revered as patriarchs of the Learning of Principle (lixue 理學)? Since the end of the Song, scholars have been habituated to conventional knowledge, mostly venerating Zhu and rejecting Lu. Confucian scholars of recent times, however, have once again celebrated Mr. Lu, holding up the "original substance" (benti 本體) to dispel the doubts of the multitude, and those in the world who discourse on learning have consequently raised the criticism that Kaoting 考亭 [Zhu Xi] pursued the external. Between these, which is truly the definitive conclusion? Now, traveling by different roads yet arriving at the same destination, the two masters indeed each reached the subtlest depths—something that shallow scholars cannot peer into—whereas those who merely feed on hearsay…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
之徒恣其雌黃以惑天下遂使講說愈
多而眞理愈晦或迷於俗學或流於異
端斯道幾何而不爲天下裂耶故欲與
諸士明辨之以定志道者之趨
問善者成性之原孝者天性之懿君子爲
善而行孝凡以自盡其性而非以徼福
爲也然天人相與之際其感應自有不
可誣者以故我
===
成祖輯爲善陰隲孝順事實二書頒行天下所
以垂世立訓者至深切矣試自爾蜀人
之列於記載者言之有行部瀨山道岷
江以祛水患有轉運廣南施方藥以療
民疾有捍徐州之河決免杭州之供米
有賑青州之民饑禦浙江之海寇有往
兩浙而減除稅畝有爲提點而禁止殺
降有爲叅軍而白無辜之冤盜有押成
都而還前掾之鬻女有造舟以濟渡有
好施而濟貧此皆見於爲善陰隲者其
punctuated:
之徒，恣其雌黃以惑天下，遂使講說愈多而眞理愈晦，或迷於俗學，或流於異端，斯道幾何而不爲天下裂耶？故欲與諸士明辨之，以定志道者之趨。
問：善者，成性之原；孝者，天性之懿。君子爲善而行孝，凡以自盡其性，而非以徼福爲也。然天人相與之際，其感應自有不可誣者。以故我成祖輯《爲善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，頒行天下，所以垂世立訓者，至深切矣。試自爾蜀人之列於記載者言之：有行部瀨山、道岷江以祛水患，有轉運廣南、施方藥以療民疾，有捍徐州之河決、免杭州之供米，有賑青州之民饑、禦浙江之海寇，有往兩浙而減除稅畝，有爲提點而禁止殺降，有爲叅軍而白無辜之冤盜，有押成都而還前掾之鬻女，有造舟以濟渡，有好施而濟貧。此皆見於《爲善陰隲》者，其
translation_en:
…followers indulge in irresponsible criticism to mislead the world. Consequently, the more discourses proliferate, the more obscured the true principle becomes; some go astray in vulgar learning, while others slip into heterodoxy—how close this Way comes to being torn apart by the world! Therefore, I wish to clearly distinguish these matters with you gentlemen, so as to settle the direction for those who set their minds on the Way.

Question: Goodness is the source of our completed nature; filiality is the beauty of ourheaven-bestowed nature. When a gentleman does good and practices filiality, it is entirely to fulfill his own nature, and not for the sake of seeking blessings. Yet in the interaction between Heaven and humankind, there is a resonance and response that naturally cannot be denied. For this reason, Our Emperor Chengzu compiled the two books Hidden Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Exemplars of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) and promulgated them throughout the empire; the means by which he handed down instructions for posterity were profound and earnest indeed. Let us speak experimentally of those among you people of Shu [Sichuan] who are arrayed in those records: There was one who toured his circuit at Laishan [?] and channeled the Min River to eliminate flood disasters; one who served as Transport Commissioner in Guangnan and dispensed medical prescriptions and drugs to heal the people's illnesses; one who warded off the Yellow River breaches at Xuzhou and remitted the tribute grain of Hangzhou; one who relieved the famine of the people in Qingzhou and defended against coastal pirates in Zhejiang; one who went to the Two Zhe provinces and reduced or eliminated taxed acreage; one who served as Judicial Commissioner and forbade the killing of surrendered captives; one who served as Adjutant and cleared innocent men falsely accused of banditry; one who was stationed in charge of Chengdu and returned the daughter sold by a former subordinate clerk; one who built boats to help people ferry across; and one who loved charity and relieved the poor. These all appear in Hidden Rewards for Doing Good; can their…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
芳名可得而盡述歟有清朝履霜援琴
而歌有誠孝事劉陳情終養有慟母感
人而位至宰相有順母出妻而地湧醴
泉有殊方念母而貯魚以遺親有三時
哀毀而免雀之呈瑞此皆見於孝順事
實者其懿行可得而盡稱歟之數人者
德脩於已福降於天以化鄉人以感異
類其故豈偶然哉諸士生同其鄉必有
景行前哲者其備述之以觀尚論之學
===
問治天下以得人才正風俗爲本先正言
之矣然有一代之興必有一代之尚而
人才與風俗因之始之所尚者未甞不
善而其流之不能無弊者勢也審其勢
而通之存乎善理者耳三代以上學術
出於一而人才風俗皆本於學之所成
後世聖學失傳各因其資之所近者以
爲人才又各因其才之所成者以爲習
俗故王霸雜用醇漓相參至宋以忠厚
punctuated:
芳名可得而盡述歟？有清朝履霜，援琴而歌；有誠孝事劉，陳情終養；有慟母感人，而位至宰相；有順母出妻，而地湧醴泉；有殊方念母，而貯魚以遺親；有三時哀毀，而免雀之呈瑞。此皆見於《孝順事實》者，其懿行可得而盡稱歟？之數人者，德脩於已，福降於天，以化鄉人，以感異類，其故豈偶然哉？諸士生同其鄉，必有景行前哲者，其備述之，以觀尚論之學。

問：治天下以得人才、正風俗爲本，先正言之矣。然有一代之興，必有一代之尚，而人才與風俗因之。始之所尚者未甞不善，而其流之不能無弊者，勢也。審其勢而通之，存乎善理者耳。三代以上，學術出於一，而人才、風俗皆本於學之所成。後世聖學失傳，各因其資之所近者以爲人才，又各因其才之所成者以爲習俗，故王霸雜用，醇漓相參。至宋以忠厚
translation_en:
…can their fragrant names be recounted in full? There was one who trod the frost in the clear morning, drawing his zither to sing; one who served Grandmother Liu with sincere filial piety, submitting a memorial to care for her to the end of her days; one whose grief for his mother moved others, and who rose to the position of Grand Councilor; one who obeyed his mother by divorcing his wife, whereupon sweet springs welled up from the ground; one who thought of his mother from a distant land, preserving fish to send to his parent; and one whose grief and emaciation through three seasons brought forth the auspicious signs of hares [?免 for 兔] and sparrows. All of these appear in the *Facts of Filial Piety and Obedience* (*Xiaoshun shishi*); can their admirable deeds be praised in full? With these several men, virtue was cultivated within themselves and blessings descended from Heaven, transforming their fellow villagers and moving creatures of different species—how could the reasons for this be mere coincidence? You scholars, born in the same province, must certainly look up to the virtuous conduct of these former worthies. Give a complete account of them, so that we may observe your learning in evaluating historical figures.

Question: That governing the empire takes obtaining men of talent and rectifying customs as its foundation has already been stated by former worthies. Yet with the rise of each dynasty, there is necessarily what that dynasty esteems, and men of talent and customs follow from it. What is esteemed at the beginning is never not good, yet that its later course cannot be without abuses is a matter of the trend of circumstances. Examining the trend of circumstances and adapting to it rests simply with those who are skilled at governance. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, scholarly learning issued from a single source, and both men of talent and customs were rooted in what was achieved through learning. In later ages, the learning of the sages was lost; each age took those whose natural endowments were close to its ideal as its men of talent, and in turn formed its customs according to what those talents achieved. Thus the ways of the True King and the Hegemon were used in mixture, and purity and dilution were intermingled. Down to the Song dynasty, which with loyalty and generosity…

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
立國號稱近古乃其究也天下之勢日
趨於弱玆其故何與我
國朝神武開基明倫立訓所以示天下之趨
者務實事而略虛文以故人才之生也
多忠誠以爲敏幹而習俗之成也亦通
達而務廉貞固彬彬然盛矣比年以來
敏幹者或少敦慤之意通達者或近脂
韋之風浸淫之弊漸失其初此又何故
耶昔賢謂立朝以正直忠厚爲本而作
===
通解者貴一善爲行之士其于慕通才
稱達節者至鄙之爲亂教賊名固皆有
深意焉可得而推之歟我
皇上踐祚之初
軫念士習澆漓官方刓鈌特頒
勑諭以昭告中外正以定所尚而全天下之才
正天下之俗也今欲上承
明命下振敝風以追隆古之盛將何循而後可
問蜀西抗吐番南控蠻夷土司環列於近
punctuated:
立國，號稱近古，乃其究也，天下之勢日趨於弱，玆其故何與？我國朝神武開基，明倫立訓，所以示天下之趨者，務實事而略虛文。以故人才之生也，多忠誠以爲敏幹；而習俗之成也，亦通達而務廉貞，固彬彬然盛矣。比年以來，敏幹者或少敦慤之意，通達者或近脂韋之風，浸淫之弊，漸失其初，此又何故耶？昔賢謂立朝以正直忠厚爲本；而作《通解》者，貴一善爲行之士，其于慕通才、稱達節者，至鄙之爲亂教賊名，固皆有深意焉，可得而推之歟？我皇上踐祚之初，軫念士習澆漓，官方刓鈌，特頒勑諭以昭告中外，正以定所尚而全天下之才，正天下之俗也。今欲上承明命，下振敝風，以追隆古之盛，將何循而後可？
問：蜀西抗吐番，南控蠻夷，土司環列於近
translation_en:
…founded its state, and was reputed to have approached antiquity. Yet in its eventual outcome, the momentum of the empire daily tended toward weakness—what was the reason for this? Our dynasty established its foundation through divine martial prowess and set up instructions by clarifying human relationships; that by which it showed the empire its direction was to attend to practical affairs and pass over empty formalities. For this reason, in the nurturing of men of talent, most took loyalty and sincerity as the basis for agility and capability; and in the formation of customs, people were likewise comprehensive and adaptable while striving for integrity and rectitude. It was indeed a refined and flourishing age! In recent years, however, the agile and capable sometimes lack an earnest and honest spirit, while the comprehensive and adaptable sometimes verge on a manner of greased-leather pliancy. Through gradual saturation by these abuses, the original state is progressively lost—what, again, is the reason for this? Worthies of the past said that standing at court takes uprightness, directness, loyalty, and generosity as its root; and the author of the Comprehensive Explanations (Tongjie) valued scholars who practiced even a single good deed, while toward those who admired versatile talent and praised adaptable principles, he went so far as to despise them as disrupting moral teaching and injuring reputation. Surely both held deep meaning—can we infer and explain it? At the very beginning of His Majesty's accession to the throne, grieving with concern that scholars' habits had become thin and decadent and that official standards had become worn down and defective, he specially issued an imperial edict of instruction to clearly proclaim this at court and in the provinces—precisely in order to fix what is esteemed, and thereby make whole the talents of the empire and rectify the customs of the empire. Today, if we wish above to uphold His Majesty's luminous command and below to rouse up decadent mores, so as to match the flourishing of high antiquity, what course must we follow before this can be achieved?

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
郊蓋三面阻夷其于邊備至急也頃者
都蠻作梗義旅徂征業巳破危巢而梟
桀虜矣孽孤殘兔將殄滅之無遺育歟
抑姑與之自新歟百年積寇行且蕩平
久安之策當亟講焉有謂移縣治者有
謂立土司者又有謂飭兵以鎮之者果
孰爲得耶卽今兵威大張諸夷落魄若
無他慮矣然松潘孤懸於絶塞建昌阻
隔於瘴鄉玀猓蠢動於峨眉番羌潛窺
===
於威疊禦之不可一日疎也將何策以
豫之歟土司復讎爭立屢搆兵端甚或
禍延內地禁治之方其將安出夫禦戎
必先詰兵乃今衛所之卒多寄空名丁
壯之選半供私役而軍需之虛冐者多
也玆欲淸理之亦有要乎內兵不足借
之土司土兵驕悍何以制之彼撫士卒
講韜略練技藝充行伍非不爲武弁聒
聒談之而實奉行以得實用者誰耶先
punctuated: 郊，蓋三面阻夷，其于邊備至急也。頃者都蠻作梗，義旅徂征，業巳破危巢而梟桀虜矣。孽孤殘兔，將殄滅之無遺育歟？抑姑與之自新歟？百年積寇，行且蕩平，久安之策當亟講焉。有謂移縣治者，有謂立土司者，又有謂飭兵以鎮之者，果孰爲得耶？卽今兵威大張，諸夷落魄，若無他慮矣。然松潘孤懸於絶塞，建昌阻隔於瘴鄉，玀猓蠢動於峨眉，番羌潛窺於威、疊，禦之不可一日疎也，將何策以豫之歟？土司復讎爭立，屢搆兵端，甚或禍延內地，禁治之方，其將安出？夫禦戎必先詰兵，乃今衛所之卒多寄空名，丁壯之選半供私役，而軍需之虛冐者多也，玆欲淸理之，亦有要乎？內兵不足，借之土司，土兵驕悍，何以制之？彼撫士卒、講韜略、練技藝、充行伍，非不爲武弁聒聒談之，而實奉行以得實用者誰耶？先
translation_en:
…outskirts; indeed, bordered by non-Chinese tribes on three sides, its frontier defense is of the utmost urgency. Recently, when the Duman tribesmen created disturbances, our righteous forces marched forth on campaign and have already smashed their perilous lairs and decapitated the ferocious captives. As for the surviving orphans and remnant fugitives—like remaining hares and foxes—should we exterminate them without leaving a single descendant, or should we tentatively grant them a chance to renew themselves? These entrenched bandits of a hundred years are about to be completely pacified, and policies for lasting peace must be urgently discussed. Some advocate relocating the county seat, some advocate establishing an Aboriginal Office (tusi), and still others advocate readying troops to garrison the area—which of these is truly the right course?

At present, our military might is greatly displayed and the various tribes are terrified out of their wits, as though there were nothing further to worry about. Yet Songpan hangs isolated on the remote frontier, Jianchang is cut off in a malarial region, the Luoluo stir restlessly around Emei, and the Tibetan and Qiang tribes (Fan-Qiang) secretly spy upon Weizhou and Die溪 [Diexi]. Defense against them cannot be neglected for a single day; by what strategy shall we prepare for this in advance? Furthermore, Aboriginal Offices repeatedly instigate armed conflicts over blood feuds and succession disputes, sometimes even spreading disaster into the interior. From whence shall come the methods to prohibit and govern them?

Now, to repel hostile tribes one must first scrutinize the military. Yet today, the soldiers of the Guards and Battalions (weisuo) are mostly registered under empty names, half of the selected able-bodied men are diverted to private labor service, and fraudulent claims for military supplies are numerous. If we now wish to clear up and rectify these abuses, is there an essential way to do so? When regular interior troops are insufficient, we borrow forces from the Aboriginal Offices; yet aboriginal troops (tubing) are arrogant and fierce—how are they to be controlled? title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
儒曰其備不在兵食而在紀綱則夫正
體統核名實而使郡邑足任優於甲兵
者尤爲要也其亦可詳之與比蜀中急
務執事者懷桑土之謀而諸生切桑梓
之慮凡有所見悉陳于篇
punctuated: 儒曰：「其備不在兵食，而在紀綱。」則夫正體統、核名實，而使郡邑足任，優於甲兵者，尤爲要也，其亦可詳之與？比蜀中急務，執事者懷桑土之謀，而諸生切桑梓之慮，凡有所見，悉陳于篇。
translation_en: … Confucians said: "Readiness lies not in troops and provisions, but in fundamental laws and discipline." Thus, rectifying the administrative hierarchy, verifying names against realities, and rendering the prefectures and counties fully capable of their responsibilities—so that they prove superior to armor and weaponry—are even more essential; can you elaborate on these in detail? As for the urgent affairs in Sichuan of late, those in charge cherish precautionary plans for securing the realm, while you students feel deep concern for your native land. Whatever insights you possess, set them all forth in your essays.

title: 萬曆元年四川鄉試錄
text:
而外脩戰守之具則吐蕃不敢窺西鄙而
邊塵淨矣土夷不敢擾內地而兵端息矣
奚獨九緣哉書曰惟事事乃有備有備無
患此千一百年常勝之道執事所謂不在兵
食而在紀綱者也夫三邊肢體也郡邑腹
心也九緣瘇瘍也去其瘇瘍則腹心固而
四肢寧此又先後緩急之辨也
廟堂經濟愚生烏足以盡之
punctuated: 而外脩戰守之具，則吐蕃不敢窺西鄙，而邊塵淨矣；土夷不敢擾內地，而兵端息矣。奚獨九緣哉？《書》曰：「惟事事，乃有備，有備無患。」此千一百年常勝之道，執事所謂不在兵食而在紀綱者也。夫三邊，肢體也；郡邑，腹心也；九緣，瘇瘍也。去其瘇瘍，則腹心固而四肢寧，此又先後緩急之辨也。廟堂經濟，愚生烏足以盡之？
translation_en: … and externally repair the implements of war and defense, then the Tibetans (Tufan) will not dare spy on our western frontiers, and the dust of the borderlands will settle; the native non-Chinese peoples (tuyi) will not dare harass the interior, and causes for hostilities will cease. How could this apply solely to Jiuyuan [for Jiusi 九絲?]? The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Only when every matter is attended to will there be preparedness; with preparedness, there is no calamity." This is the way of constant victory for a thousand and a hundred [for 千百年, a thousand?] years, and is what Your Excellency meant by saying that it lies not in troops and food, but in discipline and order. Now, the three frontiers are the limbs; the prefectures and counties are the heart and belly; and Jiuyuan [Jiusi?] is a swelling ulcer. Once the swelling ulcer is removed, the heart and belly will be secure and the four limbs at peace—this, moreover, is the distinction between what comes first and what comes later, what is urgent and what is less pressing. As for the statecraft of the imperial court, how could this foolish student suffice to exhaustively set it forth?
